name: pulse-accessibility-wcag
description: Plans, implements, and reviews accessibility for React components in this Laravel Inertia app. Use for WCAG 2.2, semantic HTML, ARIA, keyboard navigation, focus management, screen readers, touch targets, reduced motion, and accessible interaction alternatives.
purpose: Ensure components are usable with keyboard, screen readers, touch, reduced motion, and native browser behaviours.
single_responsibility: Accessibility of React components: WCAG 2.2 AA, semantic HTML, ARIA, keyboard, focus, screen reader, reduced motion, and touch.
triggers: Component has interaction, focus management, or keyboard navigation
Radix primitives, overlays, or custom gestures are involved
completion_criteria: Semantic elements are chosen before ARIA
Keyboard entry, movement, trapping, and restoration are defined
Controls are connected to labels, descriptions, and errors
Reduced-motion behaviour is defined for animated or autoplaying surfaces
validation_criteria: Keyboard-only flow works end to end
Screen reader names and states are meaningful
Colour contrast and visible focus hold in light and dark modes
failure_handling: If accessible behaviour cannot be achieved with semantic HTML or available primitives, stop and report the gap instead of shipping inaccessible markup.
Report any accessibility check that could not be verified with available tooling.
escalation_path: Route uncertain ARIA, Radix, or assistive-technology behaviour through pulse-docs-research.
Escalate to the user when an accessible alternative requires a design or scope change.
responsibilities: Define keyboard model and focus behaviour.
Ensure names, descriptions, errors, alerts, and live regions are correct.
Check reduced motion and touch target needs.
Verify accessible names and visible state with behaviour tests when interactions matter.
non_responsibilities: Visual styling beyond focus visibility, contrast, and target size.
Test implementation, though tests should validate accessible outcomes.
